learningObjective: Reason about the sources of cold-start cost (compile, load, warmup) and how compilation caches reduce them across process restarts.

canonicalClaims.claim: Cold-start cost decomposes into process init, artifact load, JIT compilation (if any), and warmup (autotune, kernel loading, cuBLAS/cuDNN handle init). Compilation caches skip the JIT compile phase on subsequent starts, and AOT artifacts eliminate JIT entirely; process init and load remain in either case.
conditions: The runtime supports either JIT with a cache or AOT deployment.
Cache keys correctly capture source, shape, device, compiler version.
nonImplications: Does not imply cached and fresh compilations produce bitwise-identical outputs.
Does not imply caches are safe across major version bumps without explicit invalidation.

misconceptions.claim: Cache hits are bitwise-identical to fresh compiles.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Autotune caches (cuBLAS/cuDNN) can select different algorithms; low-order bits may differ.

misconceptions.claim: Compilation cache eliminates all cold-start cost.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Process init and weight load remain even with a hot cache.

misconceptions.claim: AOT-compiled artifacts still pay a JIT compilation cost at first inference.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AOT means JIT is gone; only process/load/warmup remain.

misconceptions.claim: Warmup is only necessary for JIT; AOT artifacts skip it entirely.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Warmup for cuBLAS handle init, kernel loading, and clock ramp-up still applies to AOT artifacts.
